name: answer concludes the deepcopy IS needed (protects reply.result) vs. concludes it is NOT needed / mutation is safe
side_a: Credit when the answer's bottom-line verdict affirms that the deepcopy is needed (or at least that skipping it means mutating the original reply.result), i.e. it affirms the aliasing consequence rather than denying it. A conditional caveat ('if you're fine with mutating the original you can skip it') is fine as long as the main verdict is that the copy protects reply.result from the result[DATA] serialization.
side_b: Deduct when the answer's verdict denies that the deepcopy matters for the result[DATA] assignment — e.g. it says the copy is only needed for certain transaction types and that modifying result[DATA] is 'intentional and safe' — since this asserts the opposite of the required decoupling fact instead of stating it.

name: Affirms the deepcopy is needed vs denies it / declares the unguarded mutation safe
side_a: No deduction if the answer answers 'Yes, the deepcopy is necessary' and justifies it purely by aliasing between `result` and `reply.result`, without carving out cases where it is unnecessary.
side_b: Deduct 2 points if the answer denies the need for the deepcopy or restricts it to a subset of cases, declaring the mutation safe/intentional outside that subset (e.g., 'No, you only need to call deepcopy when handling SCHEMA or ISSUER_KEY ... otherwise ... safe') — the carve-out is itself a claim about what happens for the remaining transactions.

name: Type-agnostic aliasing explanation vs claiming the deepcopy is transaction-type-gated and therefore buggy for the other branch
side_a: No deduction if the explanation stays at the level of object references (`result` is the same dict as `reply.result`) and never conditions the risk on which transaction type is being processed.
side_b: Deduct 2 points if the answer asserts that the deepcopy is conditioned on specific transaction types and that the unconditional DATA modification causes side effects in the other branch — even when those other types are left unnamed/generic ('if the transaction type is different'). A generic 'other transaction types' claim counts as an implication claim.

name: explains the shared-reference/aliasing mechanism (same dict object held elsewhere) vs merely asserts 'modifying would change the original'
side_a: No deduction when the answer explicitly identifies the aliasing mechanism — that `result` and `reply.result` are the *same* object and that other code still holds a reference to it — so the mutated/serialized dict is literally the object other consumers read.
side_b: Deduct when the answer only asserts the consequence ('would also modify the original', 'prevent unintended changes to the original reply.result') without stating that the same object is shared with / still referenced by downstream consumers.

name: affirms the deepcopy is needed before the DATA mutation vs denies it / restricts it to specific txn types
side_a: No deduction when the answer concludes the deepcopy is required (or at least recommended) before serializing/overwriting `result[DATA]`.
side_b: Deduct when the answer concludes the copy is unnecessary for the DATA path or is only needed for SCHEMA/ISSUER_KEY, since it then never treats the serialized DATA as reaching any downstream consumer.
